entries.title: China's State Council issues the New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan, targeting a core AI industry over RMB 1 trillion and global AI leadership by 2030.
Microsoft invested $1 billion in OpenAI and became its exclusive cloud provider under a new multiyear partnership to build Azure AI supercomputing infrastructure.
OpenAI released the full 1.5-billion-parameter GPT-2 language model, completing the staged rollout begun with a 124-million-parameter checkpoint in February 2019.
Microsoft built a dedicated Azure supercomputer for OpenAI with more than 285,000 CPU cores and 10,000 GPUs, ranked among the world's top five publicly disclosed supercomputers.
OpenAI published the GPT-3 paper describing a 175-billion-parameter language model, roughly 100 times larger than GPT-2, trained on about 500 billion tokens.
NVIDIA announces the A100, its first Ampere-architecture data-center GPU, shipping in full production with 54 billion transistors and up to 20x AI performance over its predecessor.
NDRC and three other ministries approve the 'East Data West Computing' plan to build 8 national computing hubs and 10 data-center clusters shifting compute capacity west.
NVIDIA announces the Hopper architecture and its first Hopper GPU, the H100, packing 80 billion transistors and a Transformer Engine for large language models.
Microsoft confirmed a new multi-year, multibillion-dollar investment in OpenAI reported at $10 billion, extending its exclusive Azure compute partnership.
OpenAI released GPT-4, its first multimodal model accepting image and text inputs, available to ChatGPT Plus subscribers and via API waitlist.
Anthropic opened API access to Claude and Claude Instant, its first publicly available models, after closed-alpha testing with Notion, Quora, and DuckDuckGo.
Anthropic released Claude 2 in public beta with a 100,000-token context window, up from Claude 1's smaller window, plus file upload support.
Meta releases Llama 2 in 7B, 13B and 70B parameter sizes, trained on 40% more data than Llama 1, with Microsoft as preferred cloud partner on Azure.
Amazon agreed to invest up to $4 billion in Anthropic, naming AWS Anthropic's primary cloud provider and giving it access to AWS Trainium and Inferentia chips.
Mistral AI releases Mistral 7B, a 7.3-billion-parameter model that outperforms Llama 2 13B on all benchmarks tested, under Apache 2.0.
Google agreed to invest up to $2 billion in Anthropic, with $500 million upfront, deepening a cloud-compute relationship on top of Google's earlier $300 million stake.
Baidu unveils Ernie 4.0 at Baidu World, claiming a roughly 30% performance improvement over its predecessor and parity with GPT-4 on core reasoning and generation tasks.
Anthropic released Claude 2.1, doubling the context window to 200,000 tokens and cutting the rate of false statements roughly twofold versus Claude 2.0.
xAI previews Grok, its first chatbot, to a limited group of X Premium+ subscribers, describing it as an early beta trained over two months.
NVIDIA unveils the H200, the first GPU with HBM3e memory, delivering 141GB of memory at 4.8TB/s bandwidth, nearly double the H100's capacity.
Microsoft unveils the Maia 100, its first in-house AI accelerator, built on TSMC 5nm with 105 billion transistors and 64GB of HBM2E memory, to power Azure AI services.
Google launches Gemini 1.0 in three sizes (Ultra, Pro, Nano); Gemini Ultra becomes the first model to exceed human-expert performance on the MMLU benchmark (90.0%).
Mistral AI releases Mixtral 8x7B, a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 46.7 billion total parameters (12.9 billion active per token), outperforming Llama 2 70B with 6x faster inference.
AMD launches the Instinct MI300X accelerator with 192GB of HBM3 memory and 5.3TB/s bandwidth, built on the CDNA 3 architecture for AI training and inference.
Google introduces Cloud TPU v5p, its most powerful AI accelerator to date, alongside the AI Hypercomputer architecture for large-scale model training.
Google previews Gemini 1.5 Pro with a production context window of up to 1 million tokens, the longest of any large-scale foundation model at the time.
Mistral AI releases Mistral Large, its flagship reasoning model, ranked the world's second-best generally-available model via API behind GPT-4 at launch.
Anthropic launched the Claude 3 family (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus), with Opus posted as its most capable model on benchmarks including MMLU and GPQA, available via API in 159 countries.
Meta details two 24,576-GPU H100 data center clusters, built on its in-house Grand Teton hardware platform, used to train Llama 3.
xAI open-sources Grok-1's weights and architecture, a 314-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 25% of weights active per token, under Apache 2.0.
NVIDIA launches the Blackwell platform, including the B200 GPU and the GB200 NVL72 rack-scale system linking 72 Blackwell GPUs with 130TB/s of NVLink bandwidth.
SemiAnalysis reports Huawei's SMIC-fabricated 7nm Ascend 910B chip performs on par with or slightly ahead of Nvidia's A100 on AI workloads.

India's Union Cabinet approved the IndiaAI Mission with a five-year outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore (about $1.25 billion), subsidizing more than 34,000 GPUs of national compute capacity for researchers and startups.
entries.org: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
entries.orgId: ministry of electronics and information technology meity

entries.title: France's GENCI and CNRS selected Eviden to expand the state-owned Jean Zay supercomputer under the France 2030 program, lifting peak power from 36.85 to 125.9 PFlop/s with 1,456 NVIDIA H100 GPUs.
Meta releases Llama 3 in 8B and 70B parameter sizes, pretrained on over 15 trillion tokens, seven times the dataset size used for Llama 2.
OpenAI released GPT-4o, a single model trained end-to-end across text, vision, and audio, twice as fast and half the price of GPT-4 Turbo in the API.
Google announces Trillium, its sixth-generation TPU, claiming 4.7x the performance of TPU v5e with over 67% better energy efficiency.
DeepSeek releases V2, a 236B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model activating 21B parameters per token, cutting training cost 42.5% versus its DeepSeek 67B predecessor.
Anthropic released Claude 3.5 Sonnet, which it said outperformed Claude 3 Opus on key evaluations at twice the speed and one-fifth the cost, with a 200K-token context window.
Google opens general developer access to Gemini 1.5 Pro's 2-million-token context window, doubling the model's previously waitlisted capacity.
Meta releases Llama 3.1 405B, its first frontier-scale open-weight model, trained on over 16,000 H100 GPUs over 15 trillion-plus tokens with a 128K token context window.

Japan's METI-backed AI Bridging Cloud Infrastructure (ABCI) 3.0, built by AIST and Hewlett Packard Enterprise with thousands of NVIDIA H200 GPUs, was announced as part of a roughly $1 billion government AI-computing initiative.
OpenAI released o1-preview and o1-mini, its first reasoning models trained to generate extended chains of thought before answering, with o1-mini priced 80% below o1-preview.
xAI brings online Colossus, a 100,000-Nvidia-Hopper-GPU supercomputer built in 122 days at a former Electrolux factory in Memphis, Tennessee, to train Grok.
Switzerland inaugurated the Alps supercomputer at CSCS in Lugano, a Confederation-funded system with over 10,000 NVIDIA Grace Hopper superchips underpinning the national Swiss AI Initiative.
entries.org: Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) / ETH Domain
entries.orgId: swiss national supercomputing centre cscs eth domain

entries.title: AMD unveils the Instinct MI325X accelerator at its Advancing AI event, with 256GB of HBM3e memory and 6TB/s bandwidth, positioned against NVIDIA's H200.
Amazon invested an additional $4 billion in Anthropic, bringing its total investment to $8 billion and making AWS Anthropic's primary training partner.
Google releases Gemini 2.0 Flash, its first model with native multimodal output (image generation and multilingual text-to-speech) that outperforms Gemini 1.5 Pro at twice the speed.
AWS makes Trainium2-powered EC2 instances generally available, with Trn2 UltraServers linking 64 chips to deliver 83.2 peak petaflops of compute.
DeepSeek releases V3, a 671B-parameter (37B active) Mixture-of-Experts model trained on 14.8 trillion tokens for a reported $5.576 million and 2.788 million H800 GPU-hours.

Canada launched its Sovereign AI Compute Strategy, committing $2 billion over five years to build domestic AI supercomputing infrastructure and subsidize compute access for Canadian researchers and firms.

entries.title: OpenAI, SoftBank, and Oracle launched the Stargate Project, a joint venture to invest up to $500 billion in U.S. AI data-center infrastructure through 2029.
DeepSeek releases R1, an MIT-licensed 671B-parameter open reasoning model scoring 79.8% pass@1 on AIME 2024, matching OpenAI o1's 79.2%.
Alibaba launches Qwen2.5-Max, a Mixture-of-Experts model pretrained on over 20 trillion tokens, claiming wins over DeepSeek V3 on the Arena-Hard and LiveBench benchmarks.
xAI doubles Colossus to 200,000 GPUs in 92 days and releases Grok 3, trained with roughly 10x the compute of Grok 2.
Google releases Gemini 2.5 Pro, its first explicitly designated 'thinking' model that reasons through chain-of-thought steps before responding, debuting at #1 on the LMArena leaderboard.
Meta releases Llama 4 Scout and Maverick, mixture-of-experts models with 16 and 128 experts respectively; Scout offers a 10-million-token context window.
Alibaba open-weights the Qwen3 family under Apache 2.0, led by a 235B-parameter (22B active) Mixture-of-Experts flagship with hybrid thinking/non-thinking reasoning modes.
Anthropic introduced Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 as hybrid reasoning models, with Opus 4 priced at $15/$75 per million input/output tokens, rolled out on AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI.
Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman launched HUMAIN, a Public Investment Fund-owned company tasked with building national AI data centers, cloud infrastructure and Arabic-language models.
AMD launches the Instinct MI350 series, including the MI355X, built on CDNA 4 with 288GB of HBM3e memory at 8TB/s and native FP4/FP6 support for AI inference.
Baidu open-sources its Ernie 4.5 model family, 10 variants up to 424B total parameters (47B active), under an Apache 2.0 license.
An advanced version of Gemini with Deep Think solves 5 of 6 problems for 35 points at the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad, officially certified by IMO coordinators at gold-medal standard.
xAI launches Grok 4 and Grok 4 Heavy, scoring 25.4% on the Humanity's Last Exam benchmark without tools, ahead of Gemini 2.5 Pro (21.6%) and OpenAI o3 (21%).
Moonshot AI releases Kimi K2, a 1-trillion-parameter (32B active) open-weight Mixture-of-Experts model trained on 15.5 trillion tokens under a modified MIT license.
Zhipu AI releases GLM-4.5, a 355B-parameter (32B active) open-weight agentic reasoning model, alongside the smaller 106B-parameter GLM-4.5-Air.
Huawei publicly unveils CloudMatrix 384 at WAIC Shanghai, a 384-chip Ascend 910C cluster claiming roughly 300 petaflops of dense BF16 compute versus Nvidia's GB200 NVL72 at 180.
OpenAI launched GPT-5, a unified system that adaptively decides when to respond quickly versus reason longer, rolled out across ChatGPT, the API, and GitHub Models.
Huawei announces an annual release cadence for three new Ascend AI chip series through 2028 and unveils the Atlas 950 SuperPoD, a supernode linking over 8,192 Ascend chips.
DeepSeek releases V3.2-Exp with a new sparse-attention mechanism, cutting API prices more than 50% to $0.028 per million cache-hit input tokens.

Germany inaugurated JUPITER, Europe's first exascale supercomputer, at Forschungszentrum Jülich, co-funded by the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, Germany's federal research ministry and North Rhine-Westphalia.

entries.title: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K2 Thinking, a 1-trillion-parameter reasoning model it says cost $4.6 million to train and scored 43% on Humanity's Last Exam, ahead of GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 by its account.

Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te opened a sovereign AI data center at the National Center for High-performance Computing in Tainan, powered by NVIDIA Blackwell chips, with sixfold expansion planned with Japan's NTT by 2028.

ByteDance releases Doubao-Seed-2.0, an architecture it says is optimized for large-scale agentic production workloads, for its flagship Doubao app which had 155 million weekly active users in December 2025.

Panasonic Connect rolled out ConnectAI, an Azure OpenAI-based assistant, to all 12,500 employees in Japan, logging 55,380 employee questions in its first month.
Italy's data protection authority (Garante) ordered OpenAI to immediately stop processing Italian users' personal data via ChatGPT, the first Western government ban of the product.
Air India became the first airline to deploy a generative AI virtual agent, built on Azure OpenAI Service, answering over half a million customer queries during its pilot.
Bloomberg built BloombergGPT, a 50-billion-parameter large language model trained on 363 billion tokens of proprietary financial data, for internal financial NLP tasks.
Rwanda's Cabinet approved the country's National AI Policy, developed by the Ministry of ICT and Innovation with RURA, one of Africa's earliest comprehensive government AI strategies.

HSBC's rollout of Google Cloud's Anti Money Laundering AI cut false-positive alert volumes by more than 60% and detected two to four times more true financial-crime risk.
Carrefour launched Hopla, a ChatGPT-based shopping assistant on its French e-commerce platform, letting customers generate shopping baskets by budget or dietary need.

Emirates NBD launched a generative AI push with Microsoft, becoming one of the first companies to pilot Microsoft 365 Copilot and deploying GitHub Copilot X and ChatGPT use cases across contact centers, legal, and compliance.
OpenAI launched ChatGPT Enterprise with unlimited GPT-4 access, a 32k-token context window, and no training on customer data, with early adopters including Block, Canva, and PwC.
Walmart gave more than 50,000 corporate associates access to 'My Assistant,' a generative AI tool built on Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service.
Morgan Stanley launched an internal GPT-4-powered assistant giving its financial advisors instant access to roughly 100,000 research reports and documents.
UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak launched the world's first government AI Safety Institute, an evaluation body for frontier AI models growing out of the earlier Frontier AI Taskforce.

Google launches Gemini Business and Gemini Enterprise add-ons for Google Workspace, rebranding Duet AI and bringing generative AI to business and enterprise customers.
Microsoft invests $16 million in Mistral AI and becomes its first distribution partner, making Mistral Large available on Azure AI Studio and Azure Machine Learning.
Klarna's OpenAI-powered customer service assistant handled 2.3 million conversations in its first month, equivalent to the work of 700 full-time agents.
DBS Bank's AI and machine learning initiatives generated S$370 million in economic value for the bank in FY2023.
Moderna formalized a partnership with OpenAI to deploy ChatGPT Enterprise and more than 750 custom GPTs across legal, research, manufacturing, and commercial teams.
The Coca-Cola Company signed a $1.1 billion, five-year deal with Microsoft to expand cloud and generative AI use across marketing, manufacturing, and supply chain.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia's generative AI-powered customer messaging service cut call center wait times by 40% and resolves complex inquiries in real time.
Toyota built O-Beya, a generative AI agent system on Azure OpenAI's GPT-4o, giving about 800 powertrain engineers access to nine specialized engineering-knowledge agents.

entries.title: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight mixture-of-experts model with 896 experts, 16 active per token, and a 1-million-token context window.
OpenAI releases its GPT-5.6 model family, Sol, Terra, and Luna, with Sol scoring 80 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index while using less than half the output tokens of comparable models.
Meta releases Muse Spark 1.1, a multimodal reasoning model with a 1-million-token context window, and opens its Meta Model API to developers for the first time.
Mistral AI releases Leanstral 1.5, a 119-billion-parameter (6-billion-active) open-weight model that solves 587 of 672 PutnamBench problems and saturates the miniF2F benchmark.
xAI releases Grok 4.5, its first model built specifically for coding and agentic tasks, priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confirms the Vera Rubin AI accelerator platform has entered production, with its NVL72 rack pairing 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs.
SK Hynix confirms it has begun mass-production shipments of 12-layer HBM4 memory to Nvidia, ramping output ahead of a broader September ramp.
Galaxy Digital completes Phase I of its Helios data-center campus in West Texas, delivering 133 megawatts of critical IT load to CoreWeave under a 15-year lease.
Alibaba previews Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter model the company says trails only Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 on its own internal benchmarks.

Brazil's Banco do Brasil pilots NiCE's agentic AI copilot across a service base of more than 90 million customers, automatically summarizing conversations and surfacing engagement history in real time.
Anthropic launches Claude for Teachers free for verified US K-12 educators and begins a pilot with Detroit Public Schools Community District to study impact on teaching practice.

NHS England expands ambient-voice AI notetaking to four south-west London hospital trusts and rolls out Microsoft Copilot access to more than 500,000 staff.
El Cajon, California becomes the first city in the state to deploy an AI system, Ava, to take non-emergency police calls in English, Spanish, and Arabic, under a one-year, $74,000 contract.

notes.author: E. Johnston
notes.headline: Open-weight models from China now match closed US frontier models on published benchmarks
notes.body: DeepSeek V3 and R1, Kimi K2, and GLM-4.5 all publish weights and training details that Western labs mostly withhold. That openness makes Chinese progress easier to verify than US progress, not harder — the actual gap between the two is smaller than public discourse suggests, and getting harder to call from outside either country's frontier lab.

notes.author: E. Johnston
notes.headline: The bottleneck moved from parameters to power
notes.body: Every major 2025-2026 scaling announcement is now measured in gigawatts and GPU counts, not parameter counts alone — Stargate, Colossus, and the sovereign AI campuses in the Gulf are fundamentally energy and construction projects with a model attached. Whoever can permit and power a gigawatt-scale site fastest sets the pace, not whoever has the best training recipe.

notes.author: E. Johnston
notes.headline: Government adoption is moving faster than the public debate about it
notes.body: The US GSA's $1-per-agency deals with OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and xAI put frontier models inside the federal government within months of each company's release cycle, while dozens of other governments are still at the strategy-document stage. The real adoption frontier isn't the US versus China anymore — it's the gap between governments that signed a real deployment contract and the much longer list that only published a strategy.

notes.author: E. Johnston
notes.headline: NSF funding is a footnote next to what the labs and hyperscalers spend themselves
notes.body: Microsoft alone confirmed roughly $80 billion in AI data-center capex for a single fiscal year — orders of magnitude past what NSF disburses in AI-tagged grants. Public research funding here isn't the investment story the way it is for quantum computing; the real capital is private, concentrated in a handful of US hyperscalers and labs, and mostly undisclosed at the contract level.
